Crypto futures tied to Anthropic’s stock market debut have fallen alongside artificial intelligence stocks, but they still imply a blockbuster valuation of about $1.7 trillion, well above the $1.4 trillion the company would be worth at the top of its proposed initial public offering range.
The contracts, known as perpetual futures because they don’t expire, let traders bet on where Anthropic’s shares will trade after listing without buying the stock. That gives investors an early read on speculative appetite, though those willing to place the bets aren’t necessarily the ones who will buy the shares.

HPS Investment Partners LLC recently met with investors in New York to launch its latest flagship direct-lending fund, betting that institutional backers will keep piling billions into the leading players in private credit after a turbulent year.
The BlackRock Inc.-owned firm has begun marketing Specialty Loan Fund VII, according to people with knowledge of the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is private. The fund’s predecessor closed in 2024 with $21.1 billion of capital.

SpiceJet Ltd.’s board has approved a proposal to raise up to 55 billion rupees ($588 million), in a move that could provide a much-needed boost to the cash-strapped Indian airline.

Copper fell to a seven-month low as a stronger dollar added to downward pressure from doubts over data center demand and gloomy Chinese economic data.
Futures dropped 4% on the London Metal Exchange to as low as $12,700 a ton, the lowest intraday level since mid-April. A gauge of the dollar rose ahead of the release of minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October policy meeting.

BASF SE’s bid to consolidate Germany’s struggling chemicals industry with a takeover of Evonik Industries AG looks set to join the ranks of politically-charged deals taking shape across Europe this year.
BASF is preparing to sweeten an €11 billion ($12.1 billion)-plus offer for Evonik with more money and additional guarantees on jobs and investment in Germany’s industrial heartland, where its smaller rival is based.

item.title: MUFG: Reverse Yankees Are About 20% of Europe Corporates
item.description:
The Opening Trade • Nov 18th, 2026
MUFG: Reverse Yankees Are About 20% of Europe Corporates
MUFG EMEA Capital Markets Co-Head Fabianna del Canto says the percentage of reverse yankees, or debt issued by US companies in foreign currencies, has ballooned to around 20% of the European corporate market, with clients now looking to issue further afield markets like Australia's. She joins Bloomberg's Anna Edwards and Guy Johnson on "The Opening Trade" ahead of Bloomberg's annual Global Credit Forum today in London.

Greece’s Eurobank agreed to buy a majority stake in First Investment Bank in Bulgaria, setting in motion a mandatory offer for the rest in a deal that would create the Balkan country’s biggest lender by assets.
The Greek lender, which already owns Bulgaria’s Postbank, will Bloomberg Terminal
acquire a 65% stake in First Investment Bank from the lender’s majority shareholders for €650 million ($713.8 million) in cash. The deal values the Bulgarian bank at €1 billion.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Kenya has invested some of the $1.9 billion that Vodacom Group Ltd. paid for a stake in the country’s biggest company in government securities as it awaits the outcome of a court petition opposing the transaction, its treasury secretary said.
Two months ago, a Kenyan high court ordered that the South African wireless carrier return the additional 20% stake it bought in Safaricom Plc to the Treasury.

item.title: Xi-Trump-Putin Trilateral: A Great Power Stitch-Up?
item.description:
Trump, China’s Xi and Russia’s Putin will meet for a three-way summit this week.
It’s an unprecedented meeting that’s drawn comparisons with the summit at Yalta near the end of World War II — and raised concerns of a great power stitch-up. Rebecca Choong Wilkins has more. (Source: Bloomberg)
